Space weather outlook. Forecasters expect geomagnetic storm conditions to reach G2 on November 20, 2026, with Kp 6 predicted during the evening. The forecast is based on a coronal mass ejection observed leaving the Sun two days earlier. Arrival time is uncertain by about twelve hours. Aurora may be visible at higher latitudes if the storm arrives after dark. Satellite operators have been advised of possible drag increases. Power grid operators were also notified as a precaution. The outlook will be updated as new data from the solar wind monitor arrives. Readers can sign up for alerts on the agency site. This outlook replaces the one issued yesterday. Forecasters will hold a briefing in the morning to discuss the expected timing. Observers are asked to report sightings of aurora through the usual form.
